Youngsters is located at Youngsters Peninsula, and is located at the north of Katadelphia and Flask, near Internal Sea and Ingress. It is currently ran by TR6156Justin. The representative color of Youngsters in Los Sengas is Lime, and the District Number is 9. While it briefly became District 7 starting from January 15 2017, it once again became District 9 on March 4 2018.

Yowah Line is one of the lines in the Continuous Developmpent Phase of the Los Sengas Railway Cooperation Scheme. While the first incarnation of this line was built by Chinese Express as a means to travel along the unfinished section of Metro Line to the east of Metropolis and completed construction on June 9 2022 it is currently operated by Central-Yowah Railway (CYR). Currently, after Central-Yowah Railway announced plans to reroute within Yowah, this line has 20 stations.

History[]

Thanks to the help of various developers, Yowah has not only become the gateway connecting the Downtown Area with East Los Sengas, it also forged an interchange hub for various Co-Op Railway - Prosand. However, currently, Yowah's development pace has paled compared to neighboring regions, and various voids outside of the path of Stadium Line also exist. When Chinese Express constructed Yowah Line seven years ago, given the lack of knowledge on Yowah at the time and due to historical reasons, it only made sense that this line ran in parallel with Nazca Railway within Yowah. However, to breed new life to Yowah Line to adopt to the multi-faceted regional development mode, it is highly crucial for this line to be rerouted. With the development plan of Yowah, the north area of Yowah has the potential to become a commercial-residential mixed use developemnt zone, and this also meant the perfect time for Yowah Line rerouting. Therefore, new plans for Yowah Line has come into place, with aims of completion in two years.

  • 2025:
    • February 12: Plans for the new Yowah Line has been announced in Phase 8 of the Continuous Development Period.

Yowah Line (Rapid) is the proposed Rapid Services of Yowah Line. It is known that this line will stop at Maysang Station, Cyan Loop Station, Cyanland Station, Kong Corner Quay Station, Rhombus Sand Station and Yowah North Station, with facilities reserved for this line being built alongside the new Yowah Line, but it is unknown when this line will start services.

Line Characteristics[]

Future Development[]

  • This line will extend westwards from the current terminus of Cyan Loop Station to Maysang Station through north Greenrock Hill without going into Sava.
  • All Stations to the east of Yowah Point Station will be abolished. This line will no longer run in parallel with Stadium Line and will be rerouted to the north, before turning further north near Prosand to extend to Yowah North.
  • The Katadelphia North Depot will be bulit for Yowah Line between Candor Plains Station and Fosina Station. Crossovers reserved for the Depot will also be built.
  • Through Services will be available at Cyanland Station between Yowah Line (Rapid) and Metro Line of Peckern Transit.

This line was built by Chinese Express as a means to travel along the unfinished section of Metro Line to the east of Metropolis and completed construction on June 9 2022 with ten stations, it is currently operated by Central-Yowah Railway (CYR).

History[]

After Peckern Metro took over services of Kasukano Train Railway, there has not been any confirmation regarding whether the construction of Metro Line would be continued. Therefore, Chinese Express decided to construct this line in Period 4 of the Los Sengas Railway Cooperation Scheme. Hence, Yowah Line is born:

  • 2018:
    • March 22: Chinese Express gained construction rights of this line.
    • March 31: This line began construction.
    • April 7: The section between Fosina Station and Prosand Station began services.
    • May 13: Train speeds and arriving speeds increased.
    • June 5: Curve speeds and slope speed increased.
    • June 9: The ticket offices have been modified to get minecarts. Ticket Machines are set up at exits further from the platforms.
    • September 6: Chinese Express have gained permission to extend this line to Cyan Loop Station.
    • September 8: Cyan Loop Station began and completed construction.
    • September 9: Tracks between Fosina Station and Cyan Loop Station are paved and began services.
    • September 10 to September 12: Parts of tracks that would cause the minecart to slip backwards are fixed.
    • September 12: Passenger Information Display System inserted in Cyan Loop Station, Fosina Station, Yowah Point Station, Kong Corner Station and Prosand Station.
    • September 28: Except for Cyan Loop Station, concourses at other stations have been renovated to fit the style of Cyan Loop Station without chaning station color.
    • September 30: Level crossing added between Kong On Street Station and Kong Corner Station.
    • October 17: Connecting Passageway to Nazca Railway added in Cyan Loop Station.
    • October 28: Ticket office of Prosand Station began services.
    • December 4: All stations are graded.
    • December 8: Prosand Station platforms upgraded to fit the outlook of StarTop Railway and Element Hub Transit platforms.
    • December 27 to December 30: Platforms for all other stations upgraded.
    • December 30: Station grade system implemented.
  • 2019:
    • January 17 to January 23: Creeper Coffee added in Prosand Station. The entire line is rebuilt and electrified.
    • March 4: Elevators added in Prosand Station.
    • March 22: Departure Routine of all stations redesigned.
    • March 31: Shops added in Prosand Station while reducing number of ticket selling counters.
    • April 1: Number of ticket selling counters reduced except for Yowah Station, Fosina Station and Prosand Station.
    • April 2 and April 14: Two transfer passageway sharing fare zones added in Yowah Point Station. The station is also renovated to use a chinese style.
    • June 22: Kong Corner Station and Yowah Station are renoved to use a chinese style.
    • July 1: Kong On Street Station updated to Chinese Style and reduced concourse size.
  • 2020:
    • January 13: Riverwest Station upgraded to Chinese Style and modified to have an outdoors concourse.
    • January 17: Support Pillars to the east of Riverwest Station added.
    • February 13 to February 15: Overhead Catenaries Removed.
    • February 17 to February 18: Support Pillars between Yowah Point Station and Cyan Loop Station widened. All support pillars are at least 3x3 blocks wide.
    • February 20: Connecting passenge from Riverwest Station to Nazca Railway and StarTop Railway began services while Riverwest Station also became a Grade One Station.
    • February 22: The Chinese Express section of Prosand Station closed down and was modified as an exit passageway. On the next day, the new station completed construction and began services. Exit C distributed to Chinese Express.
    • March 8: New Cyan Loop Station completed construction and began services. Old Station Part became a station corridor.
    • March 16: Ticket offices at Yowah Station, Kong On Street Station, Kong Corner Station and Fosina Station replaced with ticket machines. Kong Corner Station station control room removed, passageways connecting to old Cyan Loop Station removed.
    • March 23 to March 24: Prosand Station, Riverwest Station, Yowah Point Station and Cyan Loop Station upgraded to SignPicture signs.
    • April 18 to April 20: Prosand Station old station concourse and platform demolished.
    • April 22: Old Cyan Loop Station demolished.
    • July 5: Yowah Station roof modified to look consistent with other stations.
    • July 8: Waiting room added at Prosand Station.
    • July 14: Prosand Station tested seal script station signs.
    • August 8: Cyanland Station renovated to Chinese Style and modified to outdoors concourse.
    • August 22: Old Fosina Station and Cyanland Station demolished and completed re-construction.
    • August 23: As most stations along the line became transfer stations and undergone major changes, the station grading system is cancelled.
    • September 9: Fosina Station added exits on the other end of the street.
    • September 20: Cyan Loop Station added connecting passages to MTR.
    • September 22: Tracks between Riverwest Station and Cyanland Station repaved.
  • 2021:
    • May 5: Upper platforms are completed for Prosand Station. This line moved to the said platform and the original platforms are reassigned for SLT Line 1601.
    • May 9: Exit A1 of Prosand Station removed. Exit A2 is modified to an elevator exit.
    • October 2: All stations used SignPicture Signs.
    • December 19: Transfer passageway in Cyan Loop Station removed.
  • 2022:
    • January 20: Exits added in Cyan Loop Station as an alternative to the transfer passageway.
    • January 22: Cyan Loop Station reconstructed to have a minimalistic style.
    • April 3: Prosand Station finished "Undergroundization" and became the first underground station in Yowah Line.
    • May 21: First class service added.
    • June 7: Candor Plains Station began construction.
    • June 9: Candor Plains Station began services. It is also the first new station on Yowah Line in four years.
    • October 25: This line is handed over to Central-Yowah Railway.
  • 2025:
    • February 12: Plans for the new Yowah Line has been annoucned in Phase 8 of the Continuous Development Period.

Line Characteristics[]

  • This line used minimal amounts of redstone wire and command blocks, a rare occurrance in Los Sengas.
  • All straight sections, slopes, curves and launches have the speed of [msp] 4. This makes this line one of the fastest among the Co-Op Railways in Los Sengas.
  • The support pillar layout of this line goes as follows:
    • Glowstone + Chiseled Stone Bricks (3x3 blocks): Cyan Loop Station - Fosina Station, Cyanland Station - Yowah Point Station
    • Stone Bricks (5x5/6x5 blocks): Fosina Station - Cyanland Station, Kong On Street Station - Prosand Station.

Station Characteristics[]

  • Cyan Loop Station:
    • Uses a minimalistic structure that involves natural lighting
    • Features connection passages to other railways.
    • Features a Passenger Information Display System
  • Candor Plains Station:
    • Uses a minimalistic structure that involves natural lighting
    • Features a Passenger Information Display System
    • Features an ultra-large concourse with two floors that spans the full length of the platforms. The upper concourse floor also crosses the two platforms
    • Features a VIP Room and a set of restrooms
  • Fosina Station:
    • Uses a minimalistic structure that involves natural lighting
    • Features a Passenger Information Display System
    • Allows passengers to walk across the tracks between two platforms and the concourse.
  • Cyanland Station:
    • Constructed by Peckern Metro and shares structure with it
    • Adopts a modern design and stacked platforms
    • Platforms are 119m long.
    • Features a Passenger Information Display System
  • Riverwest Station:
    • Adopts a Chinese-Style and ceramic Roof Tiles
    • Adopts an outdoors concourse
    • Features a connecting passage to Nazca Railway and StarTop Railway
    • Features in-train transit software
    • Features a Passenger Information Display System
  • Yowah Point Station:
    • Adopts a Chinese-Style and ceramic Roof Tiles
    • Features a connecting concourse to StarTop Railway
    • The connecting concourse is the first underground structure constructed by Chinese Express
    • Features a Passenger Information Display System
  • Kong On Street Station, Kong Corner Station and Yowah Station:
    • Adopts a Chinese-Style, with Kong On Street Station adopting ceramic Roof Tiles
    • Allows passengers to walk across the tracks between two platforms and the concourse.
    • Features a level crossing between Kong On Street and Kong Corner
  • Prosand Station:
    • Adopts a minimalistic style
    • The only underground station of this line
    • The only station to feature Creeper Coffee
    • Part of the new station shares structure with SLT Line 1601.
    • Features connecting passenges to EHT, STR and ACR.
    • While the connecting passage is the first underground structure in Chinese Express, it was constructed by EHT.[1]
    • The shops share structure with SLT.
    • Features a Passenger Information Display System

Passengers may also use this station to change to Element Hub Transit Hook Sand Line, Hook Sand Rapid (Yowah North Station) and Central-Yowah Railway Yowah Line, Yowah Line (Rapid) (Yowah North Station).

Fun Facts[]

  • The design of this station references Kong Corner Station. However, for this station, the color "Red" is chosen due to the fact that "Red" is usually associated with the North direction, Especially in Compasses. The usage of Red in this station also coincides with the "East Ring Line Loop Completion Series", where Red Wool is not seen.[4]

Zenoridge Station is a station on Stadow Line. It is operated by Nazca Railway (Los Sengas Division), and is located at Los Sengas Jupiter. Passengers may also use this station to change to Nawis Railway Labyrinth Line (Zenoridge Station).

Fun Facts[]

  • This Station is sister stations with Hawthorn Station.
  • This station shares structure with Nawis Railway Zenoridge Station.
  • The design of this station takes references from Ancient Greek Temples to allude to the Name of this station, which in turn alludes to Zeus, the god of Sky and Thunder in Greek religion.[2]
  • The color scheme of this station pays tribute to Flashsand Station.[3]
  • This Station is the first Station at which the Line Icon is used instead of the "Mind the Gap" Signs upon construction.

History[]

  • November 2 2022: This Station completed construction.[4]
  • November 3 2022: This Station began services.

Description[]

Zephyr Line is one of the District lines of Nazca Railway Los Sengas Division. It starts from Centopia and enters Xofa from the south.

This route is represented by Cyan Blue on the Nazca Railway Route Map, and is Line Number 11.

Currently, this route is 11.6 km long, with a total of 7 stations.

It is also implied that the namesake of this station is also the namesake of Wong E-Tech Station.[2]

Station Souvenir Hints[]

 The following text contains large amounts of spoilers. Read with caution.
  • Stars: 1
  • You can see a body of water resembling a river at the concourse of this station.
  • Swim Down it.
  • The Station Souvenir comes in the form of a carrot.

Fun Facts[]

  • This station is the first and currently the only station that is only served by a single Veloduct (Alpha Line) line.
  • This station is the first station in Nazca Railway Los Sengas Division to feature NR Shops.
  • While Nazca Railway claimed that, as this station is the permanent Up Direction Terminus of Alpha Line, Platforms 2 and 3 of this station are turn-around platforms. However, due to changes in plans, Alpha Line extends to Sand Martin Checkpoint in November 2019, turning this station into a midway stop. As a result, the two platforms changed travel directions.
  • This station is the largest single-line station in Nazca Railway Los Sengas Division.
  • The inspiration of this station is taken from Zootopia Central Station of Savanna Central in Zootopia and Hung Hom Station of the MTR in Hong Kong.

History[]

  • May 3 2016: This station began services. Alpha Line is established.
  • July 27 2018: This station finished Second Stage Upgrading Works.[2]
  • January 10 2025: The Station Banners of this station are set up.[3]
  • May 1 2025: The Station Title of this station is announced through the monthly calender.[4]
